newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals pare recent gains.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals pare recent gains.

text.p: The precious metals turned slightly lower on Thursday afternoon after posting steady gains earlier this week.
Gold attracted some selling after failing to muster enough momentum to convincingly break above strong resistance at around $384 an ounce, dealers said.
Bullion fixed at $383.00 an ounce, down from $383.70 in the morning. On New York's Comex futures market, December gold was down $0.90 at $385.00 an ounce.
But the main mover was silver, which came under pressure from fund selling in a thin market, one dealer said.
"It's all a silver move, and gold and the others have drifted off on the back of that," he added.
Silver was indicated five cents down from Wednesday's London close at $4.92/$4.94. It was still holding within a $4.85-$5.00 price range, however.
Platinum was also weaker at $386.00/$387.00 an ounce, down $0.50 from Wednesday's London close, while palladium was off $0.65 at $117.50/$118.50 an ounce.
"They were weak all along and never did anything on their own, so they're following gold and silver," a dealer said.
Gold prices started moving up from around $380 an ounce on Monday morning in a rally dealers attributed primarily to U.S.-based investment funds covering short positions.
Some physical and fund buying had been noted in early European trading on Thursday, along with Far Eastern selling.

Several dealers said gold was unlikely to move out of a $380-$385 price range until after the end-of-month expiry of over the counter options. Options provide the right but not the obligation to buy or sell metal at a given price.
Price charts suggested that unless gold pushed past $386 it could erode to pre-rally levels, whose nadir was the lowest in 18 months, some technical analysts said.
"Certainly the funds are still short of gold and they may try to push gold down on the back of silver," a dealer said.
But he noted that no important chart points have been broken on either end of the price scale.

In the event it extended its rally, however, "upside potential looks limited to the every considerable resistance in evidence above $390," analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge said in a commentary, referring to Comex December gold.
